messages:
elaine: Quick heads-up — release train handoff tomorrow 18:00 UTC. We're instituting a short resilience-focused partial freeze from 17:30-20:30 UTC to run canaries and validate fallback paths.
chris: Got it. Is this a full freeze? or emergency fixes allowed?
elaine: Emergency fixes only. Non-critical merges should wait until the window ends. Canaries will run on a slice of traffic and then ramp.
sam: Can you paste the canary schedule and targets so SRE can prep alerts?
elaine: Sure — plan below:
```
17:30 UTC: soft freeze begins (no new PRs merged to main)
17:45 UTC: deploy canary group A (5% traffic) - model v3.4
18:15 UTC: evaluate perf/regressions (15m)
18:30 UTC: if green => ramp to group B (25%), else => rollback + notify
19:15 UTC: full-shift decision point
20:30 UTC: freeze lifted
```
ida: Adding runbooks: please run `kubectl rollout status` and `curl /health` checks post-deploy. Link to runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/release-hand-off
devops-bot: @channel Canary deployment started for group A. CI job #4821 kicked off. :rocket:
sam: I'll wire extra latency dashboards and set an alert for p95 > 350ms. tagging @ryan for oncall coverage.
ryan: Oncall acknowledged. I'll monitor and be ready to trigger rollback if error-rate > 2%.
chris: One request — can we allow a rollback-only exception window for infra fixes? Some infra PRs need to land to avoid stale configs.
elaine: Yes — rollback and hotfix-only exceptions are OK with an owner and a quick piggyback test. Please ping me and @ops before merging.
ops: We'll hold a hotpatch channel open during the window: #release-hotpatch. Ops lead: julia.
sam: Copy. I'll mute non-essential alerts and create a short post-mortem template in case we need it.
elaine: Thanks all. Final note: if you plan to touch model-serving config, add a canary flag and deploy to canary first. Any Qs? :eyes: 
chris: All clear. Thanks.
ida: Thumbs up. :thumbsup:
